steps.hint: Try pairs that multiply to 15: 1 and 15, 3 and 5. Which pair adds to 8?

Now the second half. If two numbers multiply together to give 0, at least one of them must be 0. Suppose 7 times something equals 0.

That is the zero product rule. Once you have \((x + 3)(x + 5) = 0\), one bracket must be 0: \(x + 3 = 0\) gives \(x = -3\), and \(x + 5 = 0\) gives \(x = -5\). Finding the pair and using the zero rule are the whole method.

method_card.title: Solving Quadratics by Factorising
method_card.content: A quadratic \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\) usually has two solutions. Get one side to zero, factorise, then use the zero product rule: if \(A \times B = 0\), then \(A = 0\) or \(B = 0\). Set each bracket to zero. A bracket \(x + 3 = 0\) gives \(x = -3\), so the sign flips. When \(a > 1\), split the middle term first.

steps: When \(ax^2 + bx + c\) has \(a > 1\), multiply \(a\) by \(c\), then find two numbers multiplying to \(ac\) and adding to \(b\).
Split the middle term with those two numbers, then factorise by grouping into two brackets.
Set each bracket to 0. A bracket like \(2x - 1 = 0\) gives \(x = \tfrac{1}{2}\), so divide by the number in front.
